co_tall_green_wall.blurb: Tall Green Wall is a southwest-facing sport cliff up Phantom Canyon, a short drive from Canon City. All 13 routes are bolted, and the grades start gently: four at 5.8, two at 5.9, then four at 5.10 and three at 5.11. A few lines are two pitches, with the first pitch much easier than the second, so it suits a party wanting a mix of moderate and harder leads. The wall picks up sun in the late morning and stays warm through the afternoon, which makes it a better pick for cooler days. Routes are reached by walking uphill along the base. It feels remote despite being easy to reach from town.

co_vista_crag.blurb: Vista Crag sits high in Poudre Canyon, past Rustic northwest of Fort Collins, at roughly 8,500 feet. It is a hard sport venue: twelve bolted lines and one trad route, with grades running from 5.11 up through 5.14. Climbs are steep and strenuous, and tend to feel stiffer than their numbers suggest. The stone is pale and calcite-streaked, with orange staining, and often described as especially pretty for the canyon. Expect a long, steep hike on a faint cairned trail to reach it, and expect to have the place largely to yourself. Ticks can be a nuisance in spring.

co_second_buttress_3.blurb: Second Buttress is the central of the three buttresses on the west side of Mt. Thorodin in Golden Gate Canyon State Park, near Golden, at about 10,200 feet by one listing. It holds all 13 of its routes as trad lines, with grades from easy fifth class through 5.10: three near 5.7, four at 5.8, three at 5.9 and three at 5.10. Expect cracks, flakes and slabs, from short one-pitch lines to multi-pitch outings of several hundred feet, plus some scrambling to reach the start of climbs. Descent is by rappel or walking off, depending on the route. Late-afternoon shade helps on hot summer days.

co_sports_wall_the.blurb: The Sports Wall is a roadside cliff in Clear Creek Canyon, just west of Golden, in the canyon's Tunnel 1 sector. Despite the name it leans trad: nine trad routes and four sport. Grades range widely, from a single easy 5.5 up through 5.12, with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.11 range. It is a convenient after-work stop with a short, maintained trail walk from the parking area. Afternoon sun reaches the face and it cools quickly as light fades. Rock quality is uneven in spots, so test holds and check gear.
